description:
REDTWIN SCOUT is an independent research and software project exploring Earth–Mars terrain analogues using open NASA and USGS scientific data.

Our goal is to develop an explainable AI system that analyzes planetary terrain measurements, identifies similar environments on Earth, and presents scientifically supported results through interactive maps and visualizations.

Interests: Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Python, Geospatial Analysis, Earth Science and Planetary Exploration.
summary:
REDTWIN SCOUT is a terrain-comparison tool we built to look for places on Earth that share measurable surface features with Mars.

We started with Gale Crater and compared it with terrain in Ethiopia’s Afar region and Chile’s Atacama Desert. Using MOLA elevation and observation-count data for Mars and SRTM elevation data for Earth, we brought the terrain grids to a similar spatial scale and measured six features, including relief, slope and roughness.

Our first search evaluated 36 overlapping Earth terrain windows. The closest result was in Afar, with a standardized distance of 8.4377; Atacama’s best result scored 9.2129.

These are early results, not proof that either place is identical to Mars or safe for landing. Only 29.11% of the Gale reference cells have direct MOLA observations, so this limitation is shown in the project. This version focuses on Mars; lunar comparisons remain future work.
details:
What we built

REDTWIN SCOUT started with a simple question: when researchers need to test equipment and methods for exploring another planet, how can they find useful places on Earth based on actual terrain measurements?

For our first version, we chose Gale Crater on Mars as the reference and looked at two Earth regions: Afar in Ethiopia and the Atacama Desert in Chile.

We used elevation data from MOLA for Mars and SRTM for Earth. We brought the datasets to a similar spatial scale, then measured six terrain features: elevation variability, relief, median slope, high-percentile slope, surface roughness and local relief.

We used Python, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Scikit-learn, Rasterio, GDAL and PyProj to process and compare the data. A nearest-neighbour method ranks the Earth terrain windows according to their standardized feature distances from Gale Crater.

The Streamlit application lets users explore the candidate rankings, inspect their coordinates, compare terrain measurements and view the elevation data behind the analysis.

What we found

Our first search evaluated 36 overlapping terrain windows: 20 in Afar and 16 in Atacama.

The closest candidate in this run was in Afar, Ethiopia, at approximately 14.1874°N, 39.8174°E, with a standardized distance of 8.4377. The best Atacama candidate scored 9.2129.

We were particularly interested in including Afar because it gives us an opportunity to examine terrain in Ethiopia using the same comparison process.

Why it matters

Earth locations can help researchers test exploration equipment and field methods before using them on the Moon or Mars. REDTWIN SCOUT is an early attempt to make the search for those environments more systematic and easier to explain.

Instead of only showing a final ranking, the application shows the measurements behind it and makes the limitations visible.

What we considered

One important issue was that the Mars elevation data does not have direct observations in every grid cell. The Gale reference window has approximately 29.11% direct MOLA observation coverage. Our current feature calculations also use interpolated elevation values, so the rankings are preliminary and need further validation.

The candidate windows overlap, which means nearby results may represent much of the same terrain. We also avoid directly comparing absolute Mars and Earth elevations because their vertical reference systems differ.

This first version focuses on Mars. Lunar terrain comparisons have not yet been implemented.

Technology

Python, Streamlit, NumPy, Pandas, SciPy, Scikit-learn, Rasterio, GDAL, PyProj and Plotly.
